data.description:
## Knowledge Needed
- Read: cortical/spark/ngram.py (perplexity() method)
- Understand: held-out validation for language models
- Review: existing benchmark patterns in benchmarks/

## Implementation
1. Create train/validation split (80/20 by time)
2. Measure perplexity on held-out commits
3. Compare weighted vs. unweighted training
4. Compare different half-life values
5. Memory usage benchmarks

## Guardrails
- DO: Use temporal split (not random) to avoid leakage
- DO: Report confidence intervals
- DO: Compare against baseline (unweighted)
- DO: Measure training time and memory
- DO NOT: Optimize for benchmark scores alone
- DO NOT: Test on training data
- EXPLORE: Cross-branch validation (train on feature, test on main)
- EXPLORE: Prediction accuracy for commit message completion

## Success Criteria
- Perplexity lower than unweighted baseline
- Memory usage documented
- Training time reasonable (<5 min for this repo)
- Results reproducible
data.title: Validation and benchmarking for git-trained SparkSLM
